title: Waiting for users to tell you something has broken
summary: Monitor whether the service is doing the job correctly, not merely whether it is online.
diagnosis: A live endpoint can return wrong, stale or unusable results. Useful observability connects task outcomes to data freshness, tool failures, costs and human review. Alerts need accountable responders and actions; otherwise telemetry is only a growing archive. Collect enough evidence to diagnose failures without turning logs into an uncontrolled copy of sensitive company information.
diagnostic_questions: Which failures could remain invisible while requests continue to succeed technically?
What would detect stale data, silent quality loss, rising correction time or unusual spending?
Who receives each alert, how will they investigate it and what are they allowed to stop?
proposed_actions: Instrument task-level outcomes and key dependencies, including freshness, tool effects, cost and review queues; distinguish technical completion from acceptance.
Define service expectations and alerts tied to actionable failure conditions, with named responders and an escalation route.
Use sampled expert checks and relevant regression tests where quality is not directly observable; protect and limit sensitive traces.
working_artifact: Operational dashboard specification: task outcome; system status; data freshness; quality sample; tool errors; cost; review queue; configuration version; alert threshold; responder; playbook; privacy controls.
measures: Time from an injected or real failure to detection, diagnosis and containment.
Accepted-task quality and error patterns over time, including difficult-case and source-change segments.
Alert usefulness and unowned alerts, alongside retention and access compliance for monitoring data.
tradeoff: Logs are evidence, not learning by themselves. A model’s confidence or a user’s continued use does not prove correctness. Avoid setting universal alert thresholds without understanding baseline variation and the consequences of missed detection.
illustrative_case: Illustrative application: a daily data refresh stops but the agent continues answering from last week’s records. Monitoring freshness and answer provenance catches a failure that service uptime alone would miss.
